prevention: Built on vacuous-1112, strongest first. (1) Unrepresentable in blaze: `blaze test`/`bench` count every run into one record (blaze_screen::Tally) and one rule (cli::test::refusal) refuses a run that ran no test with exit 4 (NO_TESTS), naming the selection and the nearest tests that exist; `--no-tests pass` is cargo's behaviour; every run's end says selected/ran/passed/failed/ignored/filtered out on the terminal, in a `blaze: tests` line and as JSON (544345eec3). (2) Impossible to miss in the harness: harness/v2/ran.py is the one helper a timing row or a test run goes through (fixed environment, exit status, the caller's proof that the thing ran; a row without all three is `INVALID: why`, never a number; a test run is held to `at least N`, named tests, or an exact count); integrate.py is ported to it and exits 1 on a row that is no result; unittests.py has `at_least`; report.py refuses a script with no outcome; failures.py refuses logs with no test (f714b267c5, 83f6882263). (3) Mechanically caught in the gate: blaze.yaml's ci job holds each job its tier runs to `success` (a skip is no pass), runs ran.py's selftest (29 checks, each beside its planted bug) and library.py check (83f6882263). The rule: claims-from-evidence now says a pass counts only with proof the check ran. Not compiled and not run by the lane (write-only): the main agent's combined build and tests are the proof.
